questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are logically equivalent?

- $¬A∧B$
- $¬(A∨¬B)$
- $A∨¬B$
questions.worked_solution:
Two statements are logically equivalent if they have the same truth table. So, we construct a truth table for the three given statements:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬A∧B\,$ | $\,¬(A∨¬B)\,$ | $\,A∨¬B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |

We see that only the statements $¬A∧B$ and $¬(A∨¬B)$ have the same truth table, so they are logically equivalent.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Equivalent Statements Using Partially Completed Truth Tables
questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬(P∨Q)\,$ | $\,¬P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-3}} | $\text{T}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
¬(P∨Q){{field-4}}¬P∨Q
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∨Q) & ≡¬(\text{T}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬P∨Q & ≡¬\text{T}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∨Q) & ≡¬(\text{F}∨\text{F}) \\  & ≡¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬(P∨Q)\,$ | $\,¬P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

To determine whether $¬(P∨Q)$ is logically equivalent to $¬P∨Q,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are *different* (one is $\text{F},\text{F},\text{F},\text{T}$, while the other is $\text{T},\text{F},\text{T},\text{T}$). Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
¬(P∨Q)\text{⧸}≢¬P∨Q.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,P∨(Q∧¬(P∧¬Q))\,$ | $\,P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-1}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-3}} |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
P∨(Q∧¬(P∧¬Q)){{field-4}}P∨Q
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P∨(Q∧¬(P∧¬Q)) & ≡\text{T}∨(\text{F}∧¬(\text{T}∧¬\text{F})) \\  & ≡\text{T}∨(\text{F}∧¬(\text{T}∧\text{T})) \\  & ≡\text{T}∨(\text{F}∧¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∨(\text{F}∧\text{F}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∨\text{ }\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P∨Q & ≡\text{F}∨\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P∨Q & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.  

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,P∨(Q∧¬(P∧¬Q))\,$ | $\,P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

To determine whether $P∨(Q∧¬(P∧¬Q))$ is logically equivalent to $P∨Q,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{T},\text{T},\text{T},\text{F}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
P∨(Q∧¬(P∧¬Q))≡P∨Q.
$$
